entry.title: Driving Atomic Spins through Their Substrate Electrons
entry.summary: Coherent control of single spins on surfaces has relied on decoupling them from the substrate with insulating films, which protects the spin but also removes any electronic means of addressing it. Here we show that a local electric potential can drive an adatom spin through the substrate electrons themselves. An exact reciprocity relation fixes the torque, which equals the change of the local electron density when the moment rotates; the drive map is thus a ground-state property that can be measured independently. The relation also implies sharp selection rules, since point-contact spins, spin-$1/2$ and the central transition of half-integer spins remain dark. On a normal metal the hybridization responsible for the drive also destroys coherence, but on a superconductor the drive survives while substrate damping is confined to subgap transitions. For atomically sharp tips we find Rabi frequencies of several MHz at RF amplitudes of tens of mV, with substrate-limited linewidths below $0.1$~MHz, so that strong hybridization, usually the enemy of spin coherence, becomes an asset.

entry.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
entry.summary: The Cosmic $γ$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. We present an indirect method for probing isotropic emission from soft X-rays to $γ$-rays through scattered emission in Jupiter's atmosphere. Using archival observations from SPI, the spectrometer aboard INTEGRAL, spanning 22 years of serendipitous Jupiter observations, we analyse the planet as a moving $γ$-ray point source in the 30 keV to 8 MeV range. Our analysis focuses on Jupiter's $γ$-ray albedo, produced by high-energy photon and cosmic-ray interactions. We performed detailed Monte Carlo simulations to model the response of Jupiter's atmosphere to incident photons, protons, electrons, positrons, and alpha particles. We simulate a 1000 km deep spherical atmosphere with 1 km shell resolution, based on Galileo probe measurements. By comparing empirical and astrophysical models with the SPI data, we find no statistically significant emission from Jupiter. We derive $2σ$ upper limits across the 30 keV to 8 MeV band, which we compare with cutoff power-law, reflected CGB, cosmic-ray-induced, and long-lived mediator dark matter models. We constrain Jupiter's bremsstrahlung luminosity in the MeV range to $10^{18}$ erg/s, close to that inferred from in situ measurements obtained by Juno/JEDI. While the expected emission from the CGB and cosmic rays is a factor of $10^4$ and 100 below our upper limits, respectively, this work establishes planetary atmospheres as promising indirect probes of diffuse $γ$-ray backgrounds for future MeV missions.

entry.title: Thermal Field Theory for General Equilibrium Density Matrices
entry.summary: Thermal field theory (TFT) is the combination of statistical mechanics and relativistic quantum field theory. This (book) chapter provides a pedagogical introduction to (and a review of) TFT for general equilibrium density matrices, which allow arbitrary values not only of temperature and chemical potentials, but also of average angular momentum. A general technique to compute ensemble averages is illustrated. Path-integral methods are developed to study the partition function and the thermal Green's functions of general operators, with an arbitrary number of points, in all field theories of physical relevance.

entry.title: On deforming and breaking integrability
entry.summary: In this paper we study nearest-neighbour deformations of integrable models. After expanding in the deformation parameter, we identify four possible types of deformations. First there are deformations that simply break or preserve integrability. Then we find two different subtle cases. The first case is where the deformation is only integrable if all orders of the deformation parameter are taken into account. An example of these are the long-range deformations that appear in holographic models. The second case is when the deformation is perturbatively integrable to some order in the deformation parameter but can not be extended to an integrable model. In this paper we work this out for the XXZ spin chain and discuss the level statistics of each of these cases. We find numerical evidence that the onset of chaos occurs differently in each of these models. For the perturbatively integrable models, we find that the deformation strength at which chaos appears demonstrates a volume-scaling intermediate between strong and weak integrability breaking models.

entry.title: Matter Spectral Functions from Quantum Gravity
entry.summary: We investigate Lorentzian quantum gravity coupled to a template matter sector with gauge fields, scalars and fermions. In the absence of quantised gravity, the matter sector by itself is renormalisable, but UV-incomplete. Provided quantum gravity offers an asymptotically safe UV-completion, we determine the photon and scalar two-point functions in the presence of gravitational fluctuations, and show that both possess a Källén-Lehmann spectral representation. Our results are achieved using functional renormalisation adapted for theories in Lorentzian signature. We explain why and how interactions with gravity modify both the infrared as well as the ultraviolet behaviour of matter spectral functions. We further determine the corresponding form factors on the level of the quantum effective action. Limitations and extensions of our study are discussed alongside implications for particle physics and unitarity of quantum gravity with matter.

entry.title: Coexistence of antiferromagnetism and topological $s+d+id$ superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers
entry.summary: We investigate the interplay between antiferromagnetism and topological superconductivity in twisted cuprate bilayers. We demonstrate how topological $s+d+id$ superconductivity is induced by a twist of $θ\sim 45^\circ$ in a microscopic $t$-$J$ type model of cuprate bilayers, where it robustly coexists with antiferromagnetic order at low hole doping. This novel pairing state becomes physically accessible at realistic interlayer couplings in the overdoped regime. Crucially, it displays a characteristic $2$-fold rotational symmetry in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) not observed in the competing time-reversal symmetry breaking $d+id$ or $s+id$ states previously found. A finite Josephson effect at $45^\circ$ twist together with signatures in scanning tunneling spectroscopy of its two Majorana edge modes identifies this topological $s+d+id$ state unambiguously.

entry.title: A discrete model of the effects of inhomogeneities on the cosmological redshift
entry.summary: We develop a discrete model to study the effects of inhomogeneities on the redshift of photons propagating on cosmological scale. Inhomogeneities are modeled with independent discrete random variables at different positions along the propagation path, and the probability distribution of the cumulative effect on the redshift is computed using the moment generating function. We find that the dispersion of the distribution is proportional to the square root of the comoving distance. We then discuss what are the implications for the estimation of background cosmological parameters, giving some examples for quantities related to the luminosity distance.

entry.title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
entry.summary: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z \lesssim 1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional color-color star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z \gtrsim 2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $α_\parallel$ and $α_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $Σm_ν$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.

entry.title: Canonical quantization of all minisuperspaces with consistent symmetry reductions
entry.summary: We present the quantization of all symmetry reductions of the Einstein--Hilbert Lagrangian that correctly reproduce the reduced Einstein's field equations -- i.e., characterized by the infinitesimal group actions obeying the principle of symmetric criticality. These correspond to the spacetime symmetries of spherical/hyperbolic/planar Schwarzschild/Taub--NUT, BI/BII/BIII-metrics, near-horizon extreme Kerr geometry, swirling universe, closed/open/flat FLRW cosmologies, other FLRW-type metrics, and Bianchi type I, II, VIII, and IX spacetimes. We derive the Hamiltonian and the conformal symmetries of the superspace metrics (the conditional symmetries), promote them to operators, and solve the Wheeler--DeWitt equation with and without imposing these symmetries.

entry.title: Probing Rotating Einstein-Power-Yang-Mills Black Holes through Shadows and Quasinormal Modes: Prospects for Event Horizon Telescope Constraints
entry.summary: Within Einstein power-Yang-Mills gravity (EPYM), we build a rotating black hole via the Newman-Janis procedure applied to the spherically symmetric static seed, obtaining an EPYM-inspired Kerr-like metric controlled by the spin \(a\), the magnetic Yang-Mills charge \(Q\), and the power parameter \(q\). We analyse the horizon structure and the photon region, and we compute the shadow as it appears to a remote observer for different values of these parameters. Using the published Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87\(^*\) and Sgr A\(^*\), we constrain the Yang-Mills charge and the power parameter from the angular size and the Schwarzschild deviation \(δ\) of the observed images. At the Maxwell point \(q = 1\) the spin marginalized likelihood of M87\(^*\) bounds the charge to \(Q \lesssim 0.29\,M\) at \(1σ\), while the fixed-spin band intersection at \(a = 0.7\,M\) gives the weaker \(Q \lesssim 0.52\,M\) from the M87\(^*\) angular size alone. The bound weakens as \(q \to 3/2\), where the shadow diameter becomes nearly insensitive to the charge. The shadow radius also fixes the limiting absorption cross section at high frequencies and hence the energy emission rate, which is suppressed by the charge and enhanced by the power parameter. We then compute the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar on the rotating background from the leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) conditions on the Teukolsky type radial potential, finding that the oscillation frequency rises and the damping rate falls as the charge or spin increases. The power parameter leaves an imprint on the shadow size and its charge sensitivity and in the quasinormal spectrum the shift is in principle present but lies below the resolution of current detectors.

entry.title: Yang-Mills theories with scalar matter: a first foray using the Curci-Ferrari model
entry.summary: The Curci-Ferrari (CF) model provides an efficient perturbative framework for describing several aspects of the infrared (IR) dynamics of Yang-Mills (YM) theories. We extend this framework to YM theories coupled with scalar matter and investigate its main properties, with particular emphasis on the one-loop two-point correlation functions of scalars, gluons, and ghosts. We analyze the renormalization group (RG) structure of the model, computing its beta functions and studying the corresponding RG flows for different scalar masses. We establish the existence of IR-safe trajectories along which perturbation theory remains under control and identify a novel fixed-point, while recovering the standard CF results in an appropriate limit. We then confront our results with lattice data through a simultaneous fit of the scalar, gluon, and ghost propagators, finding excellent agreement. Our results indicate that, within the approximations considered here, the CF framework gives a successful perturbative description of the IR regime of YM theories coupled with scalar matter.

entry.title: Novel thermodynamic inequality for rotating AdS black holes
entry.summary: We propose a new thermodynamic inequality for stationary, asymptotically Anti-de Sitter rotating black holes, expressed in terms of their angular momentum, mass and thermodynamic volume as $ 4πJ^2/(3MV)<1 $. For the solutions considered, this inequality follows from the requirement that the thermodynamic identities admit a physical horizon with positive area. We examine Kerr(-Newman)-AdS, Kerr-Sen-AdS, pairwise-equal four-charge AdS black holes, charged rotating AdS black strings, and charged rotating AdS C-metrics, finding strong supporting evidence for the inequality across different horizon topologies. We then reformulate the inequality in terms of the underlying metric parameters and compare the resulting constraints with the corresponding regularity and horizon-existence conditions. This analysis shows that the proposed inequality has different physical content for different geometries. We further examine charged super-entropic black holes, for which the ultraspinning limit leads instead to a lower bound on the thermodynamic ratio. This result is consistent with the violation of the reverse isoperimetric inequality characteristic of super-entropic solutions. Moreover, when combined with the refined reverse isoperimetric inequality, the proposed bound ensures the physicality of the Kerr-AdS reference solution entering the refined bound and thereby yields the conventional reverse isoperimetric inequality. We also extend the proposed relation to higher dimensions and test it for singly spinning thin AdS black ring with nonspherical horizon topology, finding that the corresponding inequalities are satisfied throughout the thin-ring regime.

entry.title: Optimal performance of driven-dissipative many-body quantum batteries beyond complete nonreciprocity
entry.summary: Proposals for nonreciprocal quantum batteries identify the point of complete nonreciprocity, where coherent and reservoir-mediated couplings balance, as the operating point for enhanced charging. We show that, for batteries built from interacting qubits, this point is, in general, suboptimal. The optimal design is set by a more intricate interplay between the coherent coupling and the local and collective dissipation rates, of which complete nonreciprocity is only a special case. We consider a many-body battery charged by a driven many-body charger, with each qubit coupled to a local bath and the complete setup immersed in a shared engineered reservoir. For a weakly driven two-qubit setup, we prove the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction to be the optimal coupling, and show that the battery capacity is maximized at a coupling strength fixed by the local and collective dissipation rates, which coincides with complete nonreciprocity only for a specific balance between them. The shared reservoir enhances the capacity for couplings weaker or stronger than both local dissipation rates, and can increase the extractable work even where it reduces the capacity. At strong drive, with the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction between the charger and the battery, the capacity is bounded by $1/2$. For qubits arranged in a star network with a single central battery qubit, these results remain qualitatively unchanged, while the maximum capacity of a battery charged by $N_A$ weakly driven charger qubits saturates with $N_A$ in the presence of the shared reservoir, approaching its limit as $N_A^{-1}$. In contrast, the maximum capacity of $N_B$ qubit batteries charged by a single-qubit charger decays as $N_B^{-2}$.

entry.title: Chiral spin symmetry
entry.summary: We review the chiral spin symmetry, which is a symmetry of the color charge and of the confining electric part of QCD. Observation of this symmetry in the vacuum upon truncation of the near-zero modes of the Dirac operator implies that the hadron mass in the light quark sector is not due to the quark condensate of the vacuum and that confinement and chiral symmetry breaking are not directly related. Observation of this symmetry above the chiral symmetry restoration crossover suggests that QCD is still in the confining regime with chirally symmetric quarks bound into the color-singlets by the confining electric field. This regime of QCD was called a stringy fluid. At a temperature T_d that is essentially above T_ch the chiral spin symmetry smoothly disappears suggesting that the confining electric field gets screened and one observes a very smooth crossover to the quark-gluon plasma. The three-regimes picture has been further substantiated by the analysis of the N_c scaling of the energy density, the pressure and the entropy density. In the hadron gas they scale as N_c^0, in the stringy fluid as N_c^1 and in the quark-gluon plasma as N_c^2. We have analyzed the fluctuations of conserved charges that scale as N_c^1 above T_ch thus indicating a transition from the hadron gas to the stringy fluid. When N_c gets sufficiently large the three-regimes picture transforms into the three-phases phase diagram. Finally we discuss a confining and chirally symmetric model in 3+1 dimensions. This model demonstrates the chiral symmetry restoration in the confining regime and a delocalization of the color-singlet quark-antiquark systems that become very large at T > T_ch. Consequently the stringy fluid matter is a very dense highly collective system of the overlapping very large color-singlet quark-antiquark "mesons" with a very small mean free path.

entry.title: Tackling the Sign Problem in the Doped Hubbard Model with Normalizing Flows
entry.summary: The Hubbard model at finite chemical potential is a cornerstone for understanding doped correlated systems, but simulations are severely limited by the sign problem. In the auxiliary-field formulation, the spin basis mitigates the sign problem, yet severe ergodicity issues have limited its use. We extend recent advances with normalizing flows at half-filling to finite chemical potential by introducing an annealing scheme enabling ergodic sampling. Compared to state-of-the-art hybrid Monte Carlo in the charge basis, our approach accurately reproduces exact diagonalization results while reducing statistical uncertainties by an order of magnitude, opening a new path for simulations of doped correlated systems.

entry.title: Null Strings Gauged, Reloaded and Quantized, II: Null Strings on Flat Backgorund Have Discrete Spectrum
entry.summary: We continue our study of the quantization of null strings, strings with Carrollian worldsheets described by an action with two-dimensional (2d) diffeomorphisms, Weyl and Carroll-Weyl scaling as gauge symmetry. We perform light cone gauge quantization of the null strings on flat space background within Schrödinger representation, initiated in arXiv:2607.02970. We show, within the regular separated Schrödinger sector, that bosonic null strings on a flat background have no critical dimensions, have discrete, nonnegative mass-squared levels and are hence free of tachyonic modes.

entry.title: Formation of rotating supergiants via stellar mergers in dense clusters: Implications for black hole natal spins
entry.summary: We investigate how massive stellar mergers in young star clusters imprint on black hole spin distributions and the implications for gravitational wave sources. While mechanisms like hierarchical mergers and binary accretion can form rapidly spinning black holes, our central hypothesis is that angular momentum transferred during stellar mergers substantially affects the spins of the merger products and resulting black holes, with some merger products evolving into collapsar-like objects that retain thick accretion disks enabling efficient spin up. This is in contrast to the general expectation that black holes form with small spins, having shed most of their envelope angular momentum via winds and expansion before core collapse. Using roughly 150 N-body models generated with the $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ code, $\texttt{CMC}$, we analyze stellar mergers that lead to black hole formation, prioritizing ``significant'' events with mass ratio $q>0.1$. After identifying optimal candidates, we explore stellar structure and post-merger evolution implications with $\texttt{MESA}$ models to capture angular momentum injection and pre-collapse profiles most relevant for BH natal spin. In our current dataset representative of Milky Way-like globular clusters, up to roughly half of black holes are formed from such mergers, with roughly $10\%$ from ``significant'' mergers. Angular momentum estimates indicate substantial spin-up during the merger, and trends with mass ratio and stellar properties suggest strong correlations with the final black hole spin. In some cases, dimensionless spin parameters of $a\simeq 0.5$ or more are expected. This process has important implications for the dynamical formation and retention of gravitational wave sources in clusters.

entry.title: Towards a recursive construction of string scattering amplitudes
entry.summary: We construct open superstring scattering amplitudes from three-point data using the Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten (BCFW) recursion and four-dimensional spinor helicity variables. We compute the contributions of selected leading and subleading Regge families to the color-ordered four-gluon amplitude by sewing their cubic couplings and summing over intermediate polarizations. The four-dimensional description makes helicity selection rules explicit and reduces the massive polarization sums to SU(2) little group contractions. The resulting residues are expressed in terms of Jacobi and Legendre polynomials, yielding explicit sums over mass levels. We construct a differential operator relating the two polynomial kernels, including their level-dependent normalizations. These results provide a concrete starting point for organizing the infinite intermediate-state sum and investigating whether relations among Regge families can support a recursive reconstruction of the full string amplitude.

entry.title: Motion-Induced Polaron Resonance beyond the Orthogonality Catastrophe
entry.summary: We investigate the spectroscopic response of a repulsively interacting, infinitely heavy impurity moving at constant velocity $v$ through a one-dimensional ideal Fermi gas. Using an exact functional-determinant approach, we calculate the Ramsey response and spectral function, fully accounting for many-body particle-hole excitations. We uncover a strongly nonmonotonic dependence on impurity velocity: decoherence is enhanced around the Fermi velocity, whereas sufficiently rapid motion restores a narrow, long-lived polaron resonance. A long-time wave-packet analysis yields analytical expressions for the polaron energy and decay rate over the full velocity range and quantitatively captures the numerical results. At high velocity, the polaron energy approaches the mean-field value, the decay rate vanishes as $1/v$, and the spectral weight approaches unity. Thus, rapid prescribed motion provides a dynamical route to suppressing the orthogonality catastrophe and restoring polaron coherence even for an infinitely heavy impurity, where recoil is entirely absent.

entry.title: The Spectral Edge at Large Central Charge and Black Hole Statistics
entry.summary: We introduce a new approach to high-energy spectra in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, addressing the open challenge of incorporating spectral statistics into the modular bootstrap. Using the analytic theory of $L$-functions attached to two-dimensional CFTs, we leverage modular constraints among high-energy states to derive a sum rule relating the spectral edge to bulk spectral fluctuations. As an application, we establish a refined modular bootstrap bound: letting $Δ_1$ be the conformal dimension of the lightest excited Virasoro primary of a unitary CFT of central charge $c$, we show that $Δ_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq o(c)$, with at most one exceptional value of the scalar gap at each sufficiently large $c$. The result applies to theories with logarithmic rigidity of spectral counting fluctuations, as in random matrix theory. We exhibit circumstances under which the bound is strengthened further.

entry.title: Roadmap on Nanoscale Superconductivity for Quantum Technologies
entry.summary: In 2025, the Year of Quantum Science and Technology, we celebrate a century of quantum mechanics, witnessing a surge in activities that illuminate its inherent strangeness and drive technological innovation. Superconductivity, discovered 114 years ago, stands as a prime example, offering direct and compelling evidence of macroscopic quantum phenomena. Beyond its ability to conduct immense currents without loss, superconductivity reveals the quantum realm operating on a scale we can directly observe and manipulate. The macroscopic quantum coherence, where an ensemble of particles is described by a single wave function, leads to remarkable consequences: dissipation-less current and flux quantization - the basic properties exploited in superconducting quantum circuit fabrication. This Roadmap has been inspired by intensive discussions and collaborations emerging from the European COST Action CA21144 (SuperQuMap - Superconducting Nanodevices and Quantum Materials for Coherent Manipulation). The roadmap outlines the network's concrete activities, driving advancements in superconductor-based quantum technologies and charting future directions. Spanning fundamental research to practical applications, the roadmap incorporates insights from industry partners developing quantum computation. It begins by exploring quantum materials, highlighting how topology and electronic correlations could catalyze a quantum leap in technology. We then delve into manipulating the superconducting phase, leveraging advancements in magnetism, 3D fabrication, and tunable correlations. Further, we showcase the advanced microscopy techniques - such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and scanning probes - used to visualize quantum behavior. Finally, and crucially, we detail the quantum devices developed within the network, and their transformative impact on modern quantum computing approaches.

entry.title: Stationary solutions in the small-$c$ expansion of GR
entry.summary: We study the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity in ADM variables up to next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO). We show that, in the stationary sector, this formulation renders the field equations more tractable for explicit solution building. The stationary equations acquire a structure, in which the leading lapse and spatial metric are determined by a closed subsystem, the NLO rotational field satisfies a linear equation on that background, and the NNLO fields satisfy a linear system sourced by the NLO data. The stationary sector exhibits both strong-gravity and weak-field branches, whose structure becomes richer at NNLO. In the strong-gravity branch, we first obtain exact vacuum solutions of NLO Carroll gravity, including the Lense--Thirring and rotating C-metric backgrounds. At NNLO, we then construct the corresponding Lense--Thirring-type and C-metric-type exact vacuum geometries. These solutions also arise from the small-$c$ expansion of the Kerr and rotating C-metric geometries around the strong-gravity background, up to $\mathcal{O}(J)$ at NLO and up to $\mathcal{O}(J^3)$ at NNLO. In the weak-field branch, we find exact Hartle--Thorne-type solutions with an independent quadrupole moment, together with exact spin-squared corrections and a mixed quadrupolar-rotating solution. We further extend the $\ell=0,2$ sector by including higher multipoles up to $\ell=4$, where $\ell$ denotes the multipole index. These results show that the full NLO/NNLO theory admits a richer stationary vacuum sector than the magnetic Carroll truncation. More broadly, the ADM formulation provides a practical framework for constructing and analyzing stationary backgrounds in the small-$c$ expansion of general relativity, and may also offer a useful framework for organizing rotational and higher-multipole deformations motivated by relativistic compact-object geometries.

entry.title: Tidal Deformability of Neutron Stars in Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity
entry.summary: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences are valuable for testing theories of gravity in the strong field regime. By measuring neutron star tidal deformability using gravitational waves from binary neutron stars, stringent constraints were placed on the equation of state of matter at extreme densities. Tidal Love numbers in alternative theories of gravity may differ significantly from their general relativistic counterparts. Understanding exactly how the tidal Love numbers change will enable scientists to untangle physics beyond general relativity from the uncertainty in the equation of state measurement. In this work, we explicitly calculate the fully relativistic $l \geq 2$ tidal love numbers for neutron stars in scalar-tensor theories of gravitation. We use several realistic equations of state to explore how the mass, radius, and tidal deformability relations differ from those of general relativity. We find that tidal Love numbers and tidal deformabilities can differ significantly from those in general relativity in certain regimes. The electric tidal deformability can differ by $\sim 200\%$, and the magnetic tidal deformability differs by $\sim 300 \%$. These deviations occur at large compactnesses ($C = M/r \gtrsim 0.2$) and vary slightly depending on the equation of state. This difference suggests that using the tidal Love numbers from general relativity could lead to significant errors in tests of general relativity using the gravitational waves from binary neutron star and neutron-star--black-hole mergers.

entry.title: Primordial non-Gaussianity as a large-scale cosmic-web bias
entry.summary: Primordial non-Gaussianity is a unique probe of the physics of inflation, but its large-scale-structure signature is difficult to measure because it appears on the largest, most cosmic-variance-limited modes. The standard view of local-type primordial non-Gaussianity is isotropic: it induces a scale-dependent correction to tracer bias, $Δb(k)\propto f_{\rm NL}k^{-2}$, on large scales. Here we show that the same large-scale response can be reformulated as an anisotropic, nonlocal environmental-bias effect. Motivated by the spectral cosmic-web hierarchy of Kitaura and Sinigaglia, we define a Hessian field $\mathcal{H}_{ij}(\bf{x})\equiv\partial_i\partial_j\nabla^{-4}δ(\bf{x})$, whose trace obeys $\mathrm{Tr}\mathcal{H}=\nabla^{-2}δ$ and therefore carries the same $k^{-2}$ enhancement that appears in the Dalal et al. scale-dependent-bias term. Diagonalizing $\mathcal{H}_{ij}$ defines four large-scale web environments, analogous to knots, filaments, sheets, and voids, although operating on scales much larger than the conventional nonlinear cosmic web. We assign one weight to each environment and test the construction with the AbacusPNG suite of local-PNG $N$-body simulations, using $f_{\rm NL}=\{-100,-30,30,100\}$. We show that these four weights reproduce the large-scale $k^{-2}$ rise of the tracer bias. We further show that existing halo catalogs without PNG can be post-processed to imprint an effective $f_{\rm NL}$ signature. Beyond mock generation, the resulting cosmic-web response motivates an observational statistic based on changes in tracer occupation of large-scale environments relative to a matched Gaussian reference, complementary to the conventional low-$k$ power spectrum.

entry.title: Rapid and robust simulation-based inference for kilonovae
entry.summary: With the next generation of both electromagnetic and gravitational wave observatories beginning to come online, rapid analysis methods for kilonova data are becoming increasingly important in astronomy. Traditional Bayesian parameter estimation using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is time-consuming and relies on explicit likelihood approximations that can break down when modeling uncertainties are significant. We develop a simulation-based inference (SBI) framework for kilonova parameter estimation using density-estimation likelihood-free inference. The framework uses a Gaussian process emulator trained on $\sim 1300$ POSSIS simulations. We demonstrate that SBI provides a rapid alternative to MCMC that is robust to likelihood misspecification. The standard Gaussian likelihood approximation fails to capture the non-Gaussian, correlated structure of emulator uncertainty; SBI learns this structure directly from forward simulations. Simulation studies show that the SBI method accurately recovers injected parameters, while the MCMC suffers from systematic bias caused by likelihood misspecification. This problem persists when analyzing AT2017gfo, where a subset of the MCMC posteriors pile up at prior boundaries and the SBI posteriors do not. The SBI framework infers a total ejecta mass of $\sim 0.087 M_{\odot}$ dominated by lanthanide-poor ejecta and excludes toroidal and peanut ejecta geometries at the 99th percentile for both components. The SBI framework generates $\sim 2 \times 10^{4}$ posterior samples in seconds.

entry.title: A Note on a High-Energy Limit of Gravitational Perturbation Theory
entry.summary: The post-Minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in Newton's constant G around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. A regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. We show that this is an asymptotic expansion. Although the series diverges we give evidence that it is Borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. As a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.

entry.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
entry.summary: The double and triple approaches of supermassive central black holes are a fairly common process in the hierarchical picture of galaxy formation. In this case, the ejection of a black hole is possible; it may carry the accretion disk and some amount of stars with it. The activity of the galactic nucleus can be restored after the ejection. One consequence of this activity is an ultrafast gas outflow, accompanied by a shock wave. We show that the acceleration of cosmic rays at such a shock is more effective than in the case of a stationary galactic nucleus due to the lower density of the surrounding gas and the higher velocity of the shock front. In this case, proton acceleration can occur up to energies of ~10^{19} eV, which is an order of magnitude higher than in an ordinary nucleus in the centers of galaxies.

entry.title: Periodic Orbits of Van der Waals Black Holes
entry.summary: Black holes in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime whose extended-phase-space thermodynamics reproduces that of a van der Waals fluid exactly form a distinctive class, the van der Waals black holes (VBHs). The timelike geodesics of VBHs are solved, their periodic orbits are catalogued, and the gravitational waves emitted along them are computed, so as to trace how the thermodynamic pressure P and the molecular-volume parameter b shape the orbital dynamics. Integrating the geodesic equations numerically yields the energy, angular momentum and radius of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and maps out the family of bound orbits. To delimit the parameter window in which the effective potential stays well behaved, we introduce a critical angular momentum Ls. Within the orbit-classification scheme, we compute the energies corresponding to rational q for several parameter sets and display the resulting orbits. The waveforms produced along these orbits are generated within the "Kludge" formalism, which makes it possible to quantify the imprint of b on the wave amplitude and on the period. Both the orbital architecture and the gravitational-wave signature turn out to be strongly sensitive to b. The dynamical behavior of VBHs and Schwarzschild-AdS (SAdS) black holes differs markedly, providing a new perspective for probing black hole thermodynamics via gravitational wave observations.

entry.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
entry.summary: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. The Bayes factor in favor of a hierarchical triple merger origin over the non-association hypothesis is $110$. However, after accounting for the priors odds, the corresponding odds ratio decreases to $0.1$, indicating that the current evidence is insufficient to favor the hierarchical triple merger scenario. GW230720\_0823 show no detectable signatures of orbit eccentricity or line-of-sight acceleration. The inferred properties of these two gravitational wave events suggest a dynamical formation channel, such as few-body scattering or gas-assisted mergers, while a primordial triple origin is disfavored. Among the proposed dynamical environments, the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus provides the most plausible site. We further derive constraints on the local rate of hierarchical triple mergers rate under both the null and candidate scenarios. Under the assumption of no detected hierarchical triple mergers, the most stringent $90\%$ confidence upper limit is $4.2\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ for $t_{\rm max}=10$ years using the GWTC-4 catalog.

entry.title: On the nature of oscillating modes of proto-neutron stars
entry.summary: Newborn proto-neutron stars (PNS) are potential targets of gravitational wave asteroseismology, the study of the (inner) structure of stars via their oscillation modes. To prepare for the eventual detection of such modes by current and future gravitational wave observatories, theoretical studies have obtained the possible spectrum of oscillations. However, there has been disagreement when it comes to identifying and classifying specific modes according to the physical mechanism that excites them. In this paper, we present a novel scheme to classify the oscillation modes of a newly born PNS surrounded by a stalled accretion shock in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Our classification is physically motivated, as it is based on the energy of the restoring forces of the mode. We investigate the nature of the modes by considering the different regions of the CCSN that they stem from. We apply this scheme to a set of 28 non-rotating 1D, 2D and 3D CCSN simulations performed with two different numerical codes and using different progenitors and equations of state. In that way, we find that there are different families of f-, p- and g-modes in the system, living in different areas. More specifically, we identify two families of f- and p-modes associated with the PNS and the shock, respectively, and two families of g-modes originating from the two convectively stable regions, one in the PNS core and one near its surface. We also find that the dominant high-frequency emission mode is the f-mode of the PNS, associated with the strong density gradient at its surface. Our classification procedure is automatic, performs consistently for all the models considered, and paves the way to systematic studies of the dependence of the mode frequencies on the PNS properties, with direct application to parameter estimation from future observations of gravitational wave signals.

entry.title: A Free-Field Realization of Boundary Symmetries in Discrete Jackiw--Teitelboim Gravity
entry.summary: We investigate a finite-periodic Miura free-field realization of the classical Virasoro--dilaton sector relevant to sl(2,R) Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Starting from a single logarithmic Cartan field, we use the established discrete Miura map and its free-field Poisson bracket to construct the lattice spin-two current. The dilaton is then realized as a periodic composite of the same Cartan variables, selected by an inhomogeneous difference equation and its monodromy condition. This construction yields an explicit induced mixed Poisson bracket without postulating an independent dilaton bracket. We examine the associated transfer problem and quadratic adjoint invariant, and test the finite Fourier algebra against the continuous Virasoro--dilaton transformation, in which the dilaton has conformal weight minus one. The construction supplies a free-field counterpart of the JT boundary transformation laws; it does not by itself identify the Miura Poisson structure with the canonical BF boundary-charge algebra.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Phase Diagrams in $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaBr$_x$Cl$_{4-x}$ under Physical and Chemical Pressure
entry.summary: The evolution of electron correlation in the superconducting state of the mixed-crystal series $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaBr$_x$Cl$_{4-x}$ was investigated by magnetic and transport measurements. Br concentrations evaluated by electron-probe microanalysis agree well with single-crystal X-ray diffraction refinement. Demagnetization-corrected susceptibility and magnetization of crystals with $x_{c(rf)}$ = 0.22, 0.24, 0.42, and 0.63 all show a diamagnetic superconducting transition. The lower critical field $H_{c1}$, determined from the deviation from the Meissner response, shows a dome-like maximum at $x_{c(rf)}$ = 0.24. The upper critical field $H_{c2}$, obtained from the first high-field magnetoresistance measurements in this system, decreases with increasing Br concentration up to $x_{c(rf)}$ = 0.42, establishing the high-field superconducting boundary on the chemical-pressure side. Combining these results with reported transport data under chemical and physical pressure, we propose a pressure-temperature phase diagram for $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$. Its double-dome-like structure has a local minimum near x = 0, where a quantum-critical point was proposed at P $\approx$ 0.13 GPa, separating a low-pressure regime of superconductivity coexisting with magnetism and an unconventional metallic state from a higher-pressure regime with conventional metallic behavior. A low-temperature resistivity upturn, previously reported only under physical pressure, is also found under chemical pressure, suggesting that spin-density-wave fluctuations may extend continuously across both pressure axes. The phase diagram overlaps with that of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ under physical pressure, indicating that chemical substitution, external pressure, and molecular substitution can be unified in a single bandwidth-controlled phase diagram for $λ$-type molecular superconductors.

entry.title: Efficient Optimization of Tensor Rings with Low-Rank Environments
entry.summary: Tensor-ring (TR) decompositions provide a natural representation of periodic systems but are difficult to optimize because the closed geometry prevents a global canonical form and leads to costly, ill-conditioned environments. Existing periodic Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) methods alleviate this difficulty by compressing long environments to a low-rank representation, reducing local operations to $\mathcal{O}(pχ^3)$, where $p$ is the retained environment rank. Here, we extend this approach to an efficient two-site Ring-DMRG algorithm and improve its numerical robustness through appropriate gauge transformations and a generalized Davidson solver. A central challenge in the two-site formulation is the truncation step, which must account for the surrounding environment. When this environment is sufficiently separable, a suitable change of frame reduces the truncation to an ordinary singular value decomposition. When it is not separable, we instead use an alternating optimization that retains the full environment. The computational advantage of tensor rings over tensor trains depends on the scaling of the required environment rank $p$ with bond dimension and system size. For critical systems, the divergent correlation length makes long-range observables remain sensitive to the periodic geometry as the thermodynamic limit is approached. In this regime, the environment rank required to reach a fixed accuracy in the observable does not grow with the system size. Ring-DMRG therefore retains the same cubic scaling with bond dimension as standard DMRG, but at a substantially smaller bond dimension. The low-rank environment construction also provides a systematic generalization of belief propagation (BP), with standard BP recovered in the rank-one limit.

entry.title: Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
entry.summary: Let $N$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.

entry.title: Angular momentum splitter effect of $d$-wave axial phonons in orbital altermagnets
entry.summary: We theoretically demonstrate that axial phonons, lattice vibration quanta carrying finite angular momentum, can host a $d$-wave angular momentum texture in orbital altermagnets in the absence of spin-orbit coupling. We consider a minimal electronic tight-binding model with $d$-wave loop-current order that breaks time-reversal symmetry. Within the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, we incorporate electron-phonon coupling via the molecular Berry curvature and show that the underlying $d$-wave orbital magnetic moment texture of the electronic state is transferred to the phonons without requiring the relativistic spin-orbit coupling. Our results expand the range of platforms available for engineering axial phonons and point to functionality unique to $d$-wave textures, including angular-momentum Seebeck and splitter effects, corresponding to longitudinal and transverse angular-momentum currents driven by a temperature gradient.

entry.title: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
entry.summary: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.

entry.title: Tidal Love numbers of wormholes as black-hole mimickers
entry.summary: We study the dynamical scalar tidal Love numbers of wormholes that provide viable mimickers for black holes, focusing on thin-shell Schwarzschild and Damour-Solodukhin geometries. Using a matched near- and far-zone expansion, we determine their tidal response in the low-frequency regime. The presence of a long throat introduces an additional characteristic scale and naturally separates the modes into two classes. Super-throat modes probe the global wormhole geometry and are sensitive to both asymptotic regions, whereas sub-throat modes probe only one side of the wormhole and effectively perceive the throat as a black-hole horizon. We derive the scalar tidal Love numbers analytically for both classes of modes and show that their dissipative parts exhibit distinct low-frequency behavior, reflecting whether one or both potential barriers participate in the scattering process. We further find that, as the wormhole approaches the black-hole limit, the super-throat contribution becomes progressively negligible, while the sub-throat response smoothly reduces to that of a Schwarzschild black hole. These results demonstrate that the tidal response of wormholes depends crucially on whether the perturbation probes the global structure of the throat.

entry.title: Optical Geometry of a Lorentz-Violating BTZ-Like Black Hole: Reflection Double and Dirac Scattering
entry.summary: We analyze the optical geometry of a static BTZ-like black-hole metric with a Lorentz-violating radial factor, distinguishing the one-sided black-hole exterior from the reflection double constructed from its optical spatial section. The optical metric is ultrastatic and has constant negative Gaussian curvature. The reflection double is smooth and complete, with a minimal circle; it is a geometric completion, not a demonstrated solution of the Einstein--bumblebee equations. We derive exact criteria for null-geodesic crossing and return, evaluate the corresponding angular sweeps, and determine the finite domain of a Euclidean surface-of-revolution embedding. Two inequivalent magnetic configurations are specified as external test fields on the embeddable patch. For a continuum graphene analogue on the doubled geometry, we derive the covariant massless Dirac operator and reduce its radial equation to Scarf-II partner equations. The full-line connection problem yields flux-normalized complex scattering amplitudes and probabilities, the resonance-pole lattice and its gamma-function residues, spectral widths and quality factors, the digamma Wigner delay, and conditional pole contributions to packet dynamics. We compare the analytic amplitudes with direct numerical integration of the radial partner equation, including their complex phases. We further separate fixed-$\ell$ from fixed-$Λ_e$ parameter protocols and audit the optical effective-mass degeneracy using Lorentzian curvature invariants, timelike geodesics, and a massive Klein--Gordon probe. Throughout, the gravitational completion, prescribed fields, and continuum scattering results are interpreted only within the scope of their respective constructions. Device-level graphene transport and a self-consistent gravitational wormhole require additional physical input.

entry.title: Quasi-hydrodynamics beyond the conventional paradigm
entry.summary: Quasi-hydrodynamics extends hydrodynamics by promoting slowly relaxing variables to additional degrees of freedom. For such a framework to be rigorously defined and parametrically controlled, the effective theory is usually assumed to retain all the slow modes of the underlying microscopic dynamics, which must be parametrically separated from the rest of the microscopic spectrum and typically arise from weakly broken symmetries. Here, we show that none of these assumptions is essential. Using the effective field theory of quasi-hydrodynamics recently derived from kinetic theory, we study three models that challenge the need for, respectively, parametric scale separation, retaining every slow mode, and a weakly broken symmetry. In all cases, the quasi-hydrodynamic expansion remains fully controlled and can be made arbitrarily accurate. This is possible because the applicability of quasi-hydrodynamics is determined not by the microscopic origin of the slow dynamics, but by the spectral properties of the kinetic operator on a suitably chosen Hilbert space.

entry.title: Pfaffian sensitivity to temporal deformations of an N=5 background in the Lorentzian IIB matrix model
entry.summary: How spacetime dimensionality and anisotropy emerge from matrix degrees of freedom is a central question in the IIB matrix model. Our previous work constructed a family of constrained classical solutions at $N=5$, including a reference configuration with vanishing temporal extent and a pre-existing $3+6$ spatial hierarchy. Here we examine how the fermionic Pfaffian responds to temporal-matrix deformations of this configuration. The background geometry determines a distinguished real two-plane of temporal deformations. Numerical analysis of the full fermionic operator shows that the sensitivity of its lowest positive-eigenvalue doublet is strongly concentrated in this plane and dominates the first-order Pfaffian response. Under stated reflection-covariance and nonsingularity conditions, the other local one-loop contributions cancel at first order when combined, so the gradients of the logarithmic magnitudes of the total local one-loop weight and the Pfaffian agree. We prescribe a temporal deformation along the projection of this gradient onto the two-plane and determine the remaining matrix components by conditional classical stationarity. The existing spatial hierarchy is modestly strengthened at quadratic order, while the spectrum changes little at the small amplitude considered. This quadratic response is independent of orientation within the plane, although the first-order Pfaffian response distinguishes such orientations. These results connect background geometry, fermionic spectral sensitivity, and conditional classical spatial anisotropy.

entry.title: Varying Newton constant, entropy and the black hole evaporation law
entry.summary: We assume that the Newton potential of a spherically symmetric body of mass $M$ is $V=-G(M)Mr^{-1}$, where the Newton constant $G$ may depend on $M$. We insert this assumption in the Schwarzschild solution. We discuss varying $G$ in the black hole thermodynamics and black hole evaporation law. We extend the Bekenstein-Hawking formula $\hbar GS=\frac{1}{4}A$, where $S$ is the entropy and $ A$ the area, to a varying $G$. It is shown that if $G(M)$ is of the form of a power-law $G\simeq M^{-Γ}$ then $G(M)S\simeq A$ is still preserved but the evaporation law substantially depends on the function $G(M)$.

entry.title: Axion cloud survival in nuclear star clusters
entry.summary: Stellar perturbations can ionize a superradiant boson cloud while transferring energy and angular momentum from the perturbing orbits. We follow the cloud after superradiant saturation by coupling its occupation to a two-dimensional, orbit-averaged Fokker--Planck equation for the stars. The evolution includes stellar relaxation, capture, orbital backreaction, and gravitational-wave (GW) emission from both the cloud and the stellar orbits. We evolve 24 models with black hole masses $M=10^5$--$10^7M_{\odot}$ and couplings $0.04\leqα\leq0.40$. Stars with semimajor axes of a few Bohr radii, $r_c=M/α^2$, dominate ionization. Stellar replenishment from the outer cluster sustains ionization over hundreds of Myr, particularly for extended clouds. Of the 24 models, 21 lose at least $99\%$ of their initial cloud mass. For compact clouds, intrinsic GW emission dominates the depletion.

entry.title: Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
entry.summary: In the extended phase space of Donnelly and Freidel, the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole are dynamical reference frames whose phase space is the cotangent bundle of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Gluing the two exterior regions at the bifurcation point leaves a single canonical pair. Within the extended phase space, this pair can be described either by Kuchař's mass and difference of asymptotic times or by the area and the relative rapidity of the two frames, which are two gauge choices of the same system. The latter is the pair of Carlip and Teitelboim, and the relative rapidity is the time shift of the crossed product construction. We quantize the frames in this gauge and construct the gravitational entangling product of the two exteriors. Requiring the frames to be causal restricts them to the semigroup $\mathrm{SL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, whose Plancherel measure yields the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the entanglement entropy between the two exteriors, together with a logarithmic correction, both independent of the ultraviolet cutoff.

entry.title: Exploring Variational Regularization of Krylov Subspaces
entry.summary: Krylov subspace methods efficiently approximate extremal eigenstates and eigenvalues of many-body Hamiltonians, but non-orthogonal bases can suffer from ill-conditioning. This challenge is amplified in quantum computing, where direct state access and thus straightforward orthogonalization are unavailable. We investigate a variational Krylov-like framework that iteratively optimizes a parametrized sequence of states to mimic Lanczos-like couplings while penalizing linear dependencies. Analyzed against exact Krylov and Lanczos on a finite Anderson impurity model, ansatz expressivity strongly influences the performance: Hamiltonian-inspired ansätze preserve Krylov-like convergence while improving the conditioning, whereas shallow ansätze remain stable but miss low-energy directions.

entry.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
entry.summary: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). Recent GRMHD simulations of BNS mergers found that the late-time fallback is approximately quasi-spherical and motivated an r-process powered thermal model for EE. However, the available radioactive-heating power may be insufficient to sustain the luminosity inferred by such a model. We therefore propose a fallback-fed secondary-jet scenario in which a fraction of the fallback material circularizes on the black-hole equatorial plane and powers the jet, while polar fallback impedes its propagation. Using a semi-analytic toy model, we follow the propagation of the jet-head through the fallback envelope and identify jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked scenarios. The boundaries of these regimes depend primarily on the circularization fraction $f_{\rm circ}$, on the jet half-opening angle $θ_j$, and on the polar refilling factor $ξ_{\rm pol}$, with the approximate scaling $\widetilde{L}\propto f_{\rm circ}/(ξ_{\rm pol}θ_j^2)$. By post-processing data from BNS-merger simulations we find that the fraction of bound fallback material that avoids prompt capture is $f_{\rm npc}\simeq0.52$, thus providing an upper bound on the circularizable fallback supply. Under suitable prescriptions for nonthermal jet emission and thermal emission from the jet head, the estimated isotropic-equivalent $0.3$--$10$ keV energies reproduce well both the observed EE distribution for the jet-dominated branch and its low-energy end for the cocoon-dominated branch. Overall, these results suggest that fallback-fed secondary jets represent a dynamically feasible and energetically consistent explanation of the EE in sGRBs.

entry.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
entry.summary: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflation. We construct the Hamiltonians from the quadratic actions and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing parameters. Although the tensor propagation speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We then calculate the Nielsen circuit complexity of the corresponding two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation between the squeezing amplitudes, while the squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Therefore, the circuit complexity is mainly controlled by the evolution of the squeezing amplitudes. For the benchmark parameters considered here, a positive coupling increases the preparation cost of the scalar Gaussian state but slightly decreases that of the tensor Gaussian state. The scalar sector is therefore more sensitive to the GB coupling, whereas the luminal tensor sector provides a cleaner probe of the pump-field mechanism. Their opposite responses provide a differential state-space diagnostic of the same EGB background.

entry.title: Carrollian minimal massive gravity and the fate of third-way consistency
entry.summary: We construct the Carrollian limit of minimal massive gravity. The limit is singular for the algebra and regular for the Chern-Simons-like data. The one divergent bracket points along the null direction of the contracted bilinear form. The Lagrangian is therefore finite while the brackets are not. The contracted curvature still obeys a cubic closure condition, forced on shell rather than identically. The third-way coupling itself, however, is removable. For generic parameters an invertible redefinition of the auxiliary field and the boost connection takes it to Carrollian topologically massive gravity up to a boundary term. The same redefinition fails before the limit. We solve for an anti-de Sitter vacuum and a Carrollian black hole, whose rotation parameter leaves the frame and survives only in the boost connection. The degenerate vector flavor metric obstructs the standard charge formula, which we replace by a canonical one. The boundary charges, obtained in two independent ways, carry no trace of the deformation. A Dirac analysis gives nine first-class constraints and no local degrees of freedom on any background. The massive graviton is removed. The asymptotic symmetry algebra is bms_3, with central charges carried by the Einstein and Lorentz-Chern-Simons terms. The black hole has two sets of thermodynamic data, each with its own first law. One obeys the Bekenstein-Hawking area law, the other keeps the Chern-Simons entropy.

entry.title: Pressure-induced symmetry breaking and polarity in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr
entry.summary: The van der Waals magnet CrSBr has emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring coupled structural, magnetic, and electronic phenomena. Yet, the evolution of its crystal symmetry and electronic states under pressure and temperature remains unresolved. To elucidate this we employ low-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman scattering and photoluminescence measurements under hydrostatic pressures of up to 12 GPa, complemented by first-principles calculations.We observe a cascade of pressure-induced structural transitions from the orthorhombic $Pmmn$ to monoclinic $P2_1/m$ phase at $\approx$ 1.5 GPa, followed by the emergence of a polar orthorhombic $Pmm$2 phase $\approx$ 6.5 GPa. The change in symmetry is accompanied by phonon anomalies and a direct-to-indirect bandgap crossover. Our results demonstrate pressure as a knob to engineer structure, symmetry and electronic properties in CrSBr in a coupled manner.

entry.title: Restoration of rotational symmetry in light-front dynamics
entry.summary: Solving the bound state problem in the framework of the light-front dynamics (with the state vector defined in the light-front plane t+z=0), one finds that after truncation - representing approximately the state vector by a finite number of the Fock components, the binding energies become to depend on projection of the angular momentum on the z-axes. This is so called violation of rotational symmetry in light-front dynamics. It is shown that the physical solution is the superposition of these states with some well defined coefficients. For a test, we also solve the Bethe-Salpeter equation and projecting its solution on the light-front, we find the wave functions which do not suffer from violation of the rotation invariance. Comparison with them of solution in the form of superposition shows that not only binding energies but also the wave functions themselves are described by the superpositions of the split states fairly well.

entry.title: Thermodynamic Representations of Algebraically Modified FLRW Dynamics at the Apparent Horizon
entry.summary: We investigate the thermodynamic description of a general class of algebraically modified Friedmann dynamics in which the physical matter obeys the standard conservation equation and the modification is encoded through a function \(g(ρ)\). By introducing a thermodynamic matter representation \(χ(ρ)\), we construct the corresponding matter variables, heat flow, work term, and horizon entropy, and show that both the Clausius relation and the first-law balance can be consistently maintained. A continuous family of representations is then defined by \(χ_λ(ρ)=(1-λ)ρ+λg(ρ)\) with \(0\leqλ\leq1\), and the physical-matter and effective-fluid descriptions as the two endpoints. The associated thermodynamic quantities transform consistently between these limits. We further show that apparent departures from equilibrium can arise from mixing quantities belonging to different representations, rather than from a genuine non-equilibrium entropy-production mechanism. These results identify a continuous freedom of thermodynamic representation within this class of modified FLRW dynamics.
entry.arxiv:comment: Substantially revised and extended. The analysis is reformulated in terms of a general class of algebraically modified Friedmann dynamics, with a continuous thermodynamic representation framework replacing the previous nonequilibrium interpretation

entry.title: Kerr Quasinormal Modes without Variable Separation: A Two-Dimensional Hyperboloidal Teukolsky Solver with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
entry.summary: We use physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the gravitational quasinormal-mode (QNM) eigenvalue problem for Kerr spacetime directly in the two-dimensional hyperboloidal formulation of the Teukolsky equation. This formulation does not require separation of variables and thus retains the coupled radial--angular structure. Such a scheme provides a prototype for calculating the QNMs of beyond-Kerr black holes for which the perturbation equations are non-separable. Sequences with increasing angular momentum are constructed, reaching close to the extremal limit. We focus on the fundamental modes $(\ell,m,n)=(2,0,0)$, $(2,1,0)$, $(2,2,0)$, $(3,3,0)$ and $(4,4,0)$, together with the first two overtones $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$. After training, the frequency at every spin is refined by solving the discretized equation for it, so that it depends much less on where the stochastic training happens to stop. Comparison with continued-fraction values shows that every reported real and imaginary frequency component of the production network remains below $0.23\%$ error, with a median deviation of $2\times10^{-4}\%$. For the fundamental modes, both components agree within about $10^{-3}\%$ up to $a/M=0.97$, and the real parts within $5\times10^{-4}\%$ at every spin. Sub-percent accuracy is maintained in the near-extremal regime, where the damping rate becomes small and the modes are longest-lived; there the damping errors grow, and the largest, $0.23\%$, belongs to the $(2,2,1)$ overtone. The results establish a non-spectral numerical route to multidimensional black-hole perturbation eigenproblems which does not match the substantially higher precision of dedicated Kerr solvers but offers greater flexibility and requires less analytical pre-processing. The proposed approach is designed to be applicable to other backgrounds whose perturbation equations do not separate.

entry.title: Lefschetz-Thimble Method to the Sign Problem in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
entry.summary: The sign problem in path integrals severely limits the application of quantum Monte Carlo methods to strongly correlated systems, whereas the Lefschetz-thimble method offers a rigorous framework to mitigate this issue. In this paper, we establish a numerical framework based on the Lefschetz thimbles for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. By introducing continuous auxiliary fields via the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, the partition function is formulated as a high-dimensional complex integral. We employ the complex Langevin equation to explore the saddle-point distribution of the effective action in the complex plane. Monte Carlo integration is then performed to compute the partition function and Green functions. Our numerical results exhibit excellent agreement with high-temperature expansions, infrared-limit solutions, and determinantal quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations, confirming the validity of our framework. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our complex Langevin search successfully captures the relevant dominant saddle points governing the SYK model in the large-N limit. Our work deepens the understanding of the sign problem in the SYK model and provides a viable non-perturbative avenue for addressing sign problems in more complex strongly correlated systems.

entry.title: Constraining the Quadratic-mode Amplitude Coupling in GW250114
entry.summary: Detecting quadratic quasi-normal modes in black hole ringdowns would provide evidence for nonlinear gravitational dynamics, while measuring their properties would enable tests of the corresponding predictions of general relativity. Specifically, second-order black hole perturbation theory predicts that their amplitudes scale with the product of the amplitudes of their parent linear modes, with a coupling coefficient that depends on the spin of the remnant black hole. This mode-specific coupling coefficient has not yet been directly measured from gravitational wave data. Here, we use Bayesian inference on the GW250114 ringdown, modeled with the $220$, $221$, and $220\times220$ modes, to infer the amplitude-coupling coefficient of the $220\times220$ mode. The inferred coefficient is consistent with predictions from numerical relativity fits and second-order perturbation theory; no comparison shows a deviation exceeding $1.3 σ$. Although the current data cannot distinguish among these spin-dependent predictions, this measurement establishes a basis for more stringent observational tests of nonlinear gravitational dynamics in black-hole ringdowns.

entry.title: Localisation of $\mathcal{N} = (2,2)$ theories on spindles of both twists
entry.summary: We consider two-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ supersymmetric field theories living on a spindle $\mathbb{WCP}_{[n_1,n_2]}^1$. Starting from the spindle solutions of five-dimensional STU gauged supergravity, we construct theories on a spindle which preserve supersymmetry via either the twist or anti-twist mechanism and admit two Killing spinors of opposite R-charge. While the study of field theories on anti-twisted spindles has already been undertaken in some detail, the advantage of our approach allows for the derivation of analogous results in the twist case. We apply the technique of supersymmetric localisation to compute the exact partition function for a theory consisting of an abelian vector multiplet and a charged chiral multiplet in the presence of a Fayet-Iliopoulos term. We compare and contrast the results for the twisted and anti-twisted spindle and find a general formula which encompasses the partition function for both cases simultaneously.

entry.title: Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras
entry.summary: We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.
